newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Dec 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.

Front-page commentary entitled "Correctly Recognising the Stock Market Trend" calls for caution, reminding investors of 1929 Wall Street crash. Commentary also blames institutions for pushing up market, wags finger at brokerages for allowing overdrafts and says nation's media have also had hand in unhealthy rise of market.
Quota for 1996 stock offers set at 10 billion yuan with focus on large and medium size companies. The quota will be carried over into the new year.

Weekend edition of same paper also says five sets of regulations on the commodities futures trading to be put in place early next year. Calls for traders to note rules barring T plus O -- or same day settlement -- procedures.
Beijing government to focus support for real estate market on housing for mid and lower income families in new year.
Interest rate subsidy on long-term bank deposits set at 2.87 percent for January, down from 3.72 percent in December.
Commentary calls for a return to "rational" investments in the nation's stock markets.

Government plans to check tide of rural labour looking for jobs in nation's cities. A Ministry of Construction blueprint calls for relocating some 30 million surplus farm workers to smaller towns by year 2000.
